strengths: Addresses a fundamental limitation of current VLA models—the lack of temporal context in non-Markovian manipulation—via an effective and principled memory architecture rather than simple frame stacking.

Well-structured perceptual-cognitive dual-stream design: decouples fine-grained visual details (perceptual) from high-level reasoning semantics (cognitive), supported by an effective gating fusion and similarity-based consolidation mechanism to bound memory growth.

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple standard benchmarks (SimplerEnv-Bridge, SimplerEnv-Fractal, LIBERO-5 suites) and physical hardware (WidowX and Franka robots across 12 distinct real-world tasks).

Particularly compelling gains on long-horizon and temporally ambiguous tasks (e.g., +26% improvement on real-world long-horizon temporal tasks and +14.6% on SimplerEnv-Bridge over strong baselines like CogACT and π0).
Thorough ablation studies justifying the contribution of both memory streams, the temporal positional encoding, gate fusion, and token-merge consolidation over FIFO.
weaknesses: Lacks explicit discussion and benchmark numbers regarding inference latency, control frequency (Hz), and memory overhead during real-time deployment, which is crucial for real-world robotic execution.

Details on how gradients flow through the memory bank during training are somewhat under-specified: it is unclear whether memory entries are detached (stop-gradient) or if the model undergoes truncated backpropagation through time over the memory queue.

The ablation results show that increasing memory length from 16 to 64 degrades performance back to the level of length 4 (67.7%), but the manuscript provides limited analysis or explanation for this degradation.

strengths: Addresses an important and practical limitation in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models: standard policies are purely Markovian (single-frame) and suffer on non-Markovian tasks with temporal ambiguity or long horizons.

The Perceptual-Cognitive Memory Bank (PCMB) design is well-motivated, decoupling fine-grained visual features (from vision backbones) and high-level semantic tokens (from LLM EOS representations), combined with a similarity-based consolidation mechanism to control memory size.

Extensive experimental evaluation across simulation benchmarks (SimplerEnv-Bridge, SimplerEnv-Fractal, and all five LIBERO suites) and real-world hardware across two robotic platforms (Franka Emika Panda and WidowX).
Consistently outperforms strong competitive baselines, including CogACT and π0, with particularly marked improvements on long-horizon temporal tasks that explicitly test historical dependency.
Meaningful ablation studies validating the individual contributions of perceptual vs. cognitive memory streams, memory length, gate fusion, and token-merge consolidation over FIFO.
weaknesses: The cognitive science framing (hippocampus, cerebellum, working memory) is somewhat decorative; the underlying mechanism is fundamentally cross-attention over a bounded key-value feature store with learned gating and token averaging.

Limited analysis on memory scaling: in the memory length ablation (Table 5), increasing memory capacity from 16 to 64 degrades performance (from 71.9% to 67.7%). The paper lacks an in-depth discussion on why larger memory capacity hurts (e.g., attention dilution, retrieval distractors) and how this limits scaling to very long episodes.

Ambiguity in training dynamics and backpropagation: Section B.3 mentions grouped sampling of 16 frames for training, but it is not sufficiently clear whether gradients flow through the memory update/consolidation process across time steps, or if entries in the memory bank are treated as detached context vectors.

In the real-world long-horizon temporal benchmarks (Table 4), the reported numbers are step-wise partial credit scores rather than binary end-to-end task success rates. While this metric is described in Appendix C.3, reporting them alongside binary success rates without explicit prominent differentiation in the main table can be slightly confusing.

Inference latency and memory footprint overheads introduced by maintaining the dual-stream memory bank and cross-attention operations are not quantitatively benchmarked against standard single-frame VLA models.

strengths: Addresses an important and practical limitation in current VLA models: handling non-Markovian, long-horizon temporal dependencies without suffering from quadratic attention explosion or pretraining distribution mismatch.

Well-motivated architecture design that separates perceptual details from high-level cognitive abstractions, incorporating structured cross-attention retrieval, learned gating fusion, and token-merging memory consolidation.
Comprehensive empirical evaluation spanning standard simulation benchmarks (SimplerEnv-Bridge, SimplerEnv-Fractal, LIBERO) and extensive real-world robot experiments across Franka and WidowX robots.
Impressive performance gains, especially in long-horizon temporal tasks where MemoryVLA achieves an 83% success rate on real-world temporal tasks (+26 points over CogACT).
Thorough ablation studies that clearly isolate the benefits of dual memory types, timestep positional encodings, gated fusion, and similarity-based memory consolidation over standard FIFO queues.
weaknesses: Lack of controlled temporal baseline comparisons: while MemoryVLA is compared against strong contemporary VLAs (such as CogACT and π0), it would be insightful to ablate against a simpler temporal baseline on the exact same backbone and action expert (e.g., naive frame stacking or standard recurrent buffering/LSTM) to precisely isolate the architecture gains of PCMB.

The memory consolidation strategy relies on averaging the most similar adjacent entries. In very long episodes, recursive averaging could potentially lead to feature degradation or representation drift; further analysis on memory retention over very long trajectories would be beneficial.

The real-world evaluation on long-horizon temporal tasks relies on a customized partial scoring metric across 10-15 trials per task; reporting standard deviation or confidence intervals would provide clearer statistical certainty.

strengths: Addresses a fundamental limitation of current Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, which are largely Markovian and struggle with long-horizon manipulation tasks exhibiting temporal ambiguity or history dependence.

Well-motivated architecture inspired by cognitive dual-memory systems: explicitly separating fine-grained perceptual memory from high-level semantic cognitive tokens avoids quadratic token bloat while preserving necessary low-level spatial and high-level task progress information.

Extensive and rigorous experimental validation across multiple standard simulation benchmarks (SimplerEnv-Bridge, SimplerEnv-Fractal, LIBERO-5 suites, and Mikasa-Robo) as well as extensive physical robot trials on Franka and WidowX platforms across 12 distinct real-world tasks.

Significant empirical performance gains over state-of-the-art baselines (e.g., CogACT, π0, and CronusVLA), particularly on tasks requiring temporal memory such as Mikasa-Robo (+11.8%) and real-world temporal tasks (+26%).

Thorough ablations isolating the impact of memory modalities, context length, gating mechanism, positional encoding, and consolidation methods, accompanied by an inference efficiency analysis demonstrating minimal runtime overhead (+3.6% latency).
weaknesses: The training dynamics and gradient propagation through the memory bank are not fully clarified: it is important to explicitly state whether memory bank updates are trained end-to-end via truncated backpropagation through time (TBPTT) or if memory entries are stored as detached representations during training.

The memory consolidation mechanism relies on simple linear averaging of the most similar adjacent entries, which could potentially blur subtle but critical state transitions (e.g., precise touch/contact moments) over long trajectories.

Real-world long-horizon tasks report composite 'success scores' based on step-wise partial credit rather than strict binary completion rates, which makes direct comparison to standard binary success metrics in the literature slightly less straightforward.

strengths: Well-motivated architecture addressing a fundamental limitation in current VLA models: the lack of explicit temporal modeling for non-Markovian robotic manipulation.

Well-designed Perceptual-Cognitive Memory Bank (PCMB) that separates fine-grained visual details from high-level cognitive tokens, complemented by an effective similarity-based consolidation mechanism to keep memory bounded and inference lightweight (only ~3.6% latency overhead).

Extensive and rigorous evaluation across diverse simulation benchmarks (SimplerEnv Bridge & Fractal, all five LIBERO suites, and the memory-focused Mikasa-Robo benchmark) as well as real-world platforms (Franka and WidowX across 12 tasks).

Substantial empirical gains over competitive baselines including CogACT, π0, and CronusVLA, with especially prominent improvements on long-horizon and memory-dependent tasks (+26 points on real-world temporal tasks and +11.8 points on Mikasa-Robo).
Thorough ablation studies and qualitative case studies clearly validating the impact of individual design components (dual-stream memory, memory length, gating, PE, and consolidation).
weaknesses: The consolidation mechanism relies on a simple pairwise averaging heuristic for temporally adjacent entries, which could potentially cause representation blurring over very long sequences.

Real-world long-horizon temporal evaluations employ custom step-wise scoring schemes; while sensible for quantifying partial progress, reporting standard binary full-episode success rates alongside step scores would facilitate clearer cross-study comparisons.

Some simulation baseline numbers (e.g., π0 on LIBERO) utilize additional input modalities like wrist cameras and proprioception, which, although highlighting MemoryVLA's efficiency with single-camera input, leaves slight discrepancies in exact apples-to-apples sensor configurations.

strengths: Well-motivated formulation addressing the inherent non-Markovian nature of robotic manipulation, where single-frame VLA models frequently suffer from temporal ambiguity (e.g., reversible actions, multi-step sub-goals).

Thoughtful architectural design that decouples memory into dual perceptual and cognitive streams, complemented by a principled consolidation mechanism (merging temporally adjacent, semantically similar entries) that keeps computational and memory overhead very low (+3.6% latency overhead, >80 Hz throughput).

Extensive empirical validation across four diverse simulation benchmarks (SimplerEnv-Bridge, SimplerEnv-Fractal, LIBERO, Mikasa-Robo) and real-world evaluations across two robot platforms (Franka and WidowX), consistently showing clear improvements over competitive baselines such as CogACT and π0.
Particularly strong gains on tasks that inherently require temporal tracking (e.g., +41.0% on Mikasa-Robo ShellGameTouch, +26% average improvement on real-world long-horizon temporal tasks).
Detailed ablation studies and qualitative analyses, including memory element retrieval attention visualizations, memory length studies, and out-of-distribution robustness tests.
weaknesses: The underlying technical mechanisms (cross-attention retrieval with sinusoidal positional encoding, gate fusion, and similarity-based feature merging) are largely adaptations of established techniques from video processing and memory-augmented networks, making the algorithmic novelty somewhat incremental.

In the real-world evaluation, the comparison is limited to single-frame/standard baselines (OpenVLA, π0, CogACT); comparing against straightforward temporal baselines (such as an identical backbone with simple frame concatenation or recurrent temporal pooling) in the physical robot setup would more conclusively isolate the specific contribution of the dual perceptual-cognitive bank over simpler history mechanisms.

Discrepancy in memory horizons across tasks: training and evaluation use a short memory length (L=16) for simulation and general tasks, but scale up to L=256 for real-world temporal tasks, leaving the automated tuning or generalizability of the memory length across arbitrary long-horizon domains underexplored.

Potential feature degradation from the consolidation rule (Equation 9): repeatedly taking the simple average of adjacent tokens over very long horizons (e.g., unfiltered real trajectories exceeding 1,000 steps) risks information smoothing/dilution of early critical events, which lacks detailed error or degradation analysis.
